newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE shares mixed in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE shares mixed in Beirut.

text.p: SOLIDERE shares were mixed on reduced turnover on Wednesday -- the third day of trade on the official Beirut Stock exchange (BSE).
A shares, distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district which the company is rebuilding, rose to $115 from $113 on Tuesday.
B shares, issued in a $650 million flotation in January 1994, fell to $115.75 from $120.
Turnover fell to 3,315 shares from Tuesday's 5,192 and the value of traded SOLIDERE shares was $384,112 from $606,009.
There was no trade in any of the three other listed companies: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
On Tuesday, 3,000 shares were traded at $1.3125, unchanged from September 20.
Dealers say the SOLIDERE switch from the privately-operated Beirut Secondary Market is positive for the development of Lebanon's re-emerging capital markets.
The move added some $2 billion to the capitalisation of the BSE, which had a total capitalisation of below $400 million.
The LISPI stock index fell 0.26 percent to 84.48 and BLOM stock index fell 0.84 percent to 981.20.
